title: The Alibi of Saint Alder's Again
premise: Ulyana Dravenmoor, coroner of fog-bound Saint Alder's, receives two letters the same morning: one from a dying man confessing to a murder thirty years old, and one from an anonymous sender promising 'the next one at the anniversary dinner.' As the town's founding families gather to celebrate the Saint Alder's Founders' Trust's thirtieth year, Ulyana discovers the confession is a forgery — but a forgery built from a real crime, one the Trust's heirs buried to secure their inheritance. When a second death strikes at the dinner itself, Ulyana realizes the killer is completing a pattern begun decades ago, punishing each heir for what they did to survive one terrible winter night. The killer is Ulyana's own mentor, the retired coroner who signed the original death certificate and has watched the lie fester for thirty years; in the final confrontation at the old chapel crypt, Ulyana must choose between exposing him and protecting the town's last shreds of peace — and chooses truth, at the cost of everything they thought Saint Alder's was.
about_author: Juniper Vane is the pen name of a former small-town records clerk who spent years cataloguing the quiet cruelties of close-knit communities. They write mysteries where the dead are remembered more honestly than the living care to be.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Between autopsies in the basement morgue, Ulyana opens two letters: Elias Marsh's deathbed confession to killing Ada Wrenlow in 1995, and an anonymous note promising 'the next one at the anniversary dinner.' The emotional beat is cold unease — Ulyana knows Elias is too weak to hold a pen, and Ada's grave has been empty for years. They begin pulling old files against their better judgment.

chapters.title: The Empty Grave
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Ulyana exhumes records and finds Ada Wrenlow's coffin contains stones, her death certificate signed by Ulyana's mentor, retired coroner Ambrose Kettle. The Founders' Trust heirs — the Voss, Crane, and Bellamy families — all have alibis from that night, airtight and identical in their phrasing. The beat is creeping dread: someone coached these people, and only a coroner could have.

chapters.title: Heirs and Alibis
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Ulyana interviews the heirs before the anniversary dinner, watching each rehearse the same thirty-year-old story. Matriarch Odile Voss is defiant, the Crane son drinks, young Ivy Bellamy seems genuinely frightened. The beat is the corruption of inheritance — each heir has profited from Ada's erasure, and each fears the letters mean exposure.

chapters.title: What Ambrose Kept
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Searching Ambrose's shuttered cottage, Ulyana finds his old case journals with pages razored out and a photograph of five young people — the heirs plus Ada — dated the week she vanished. Ambrose, when confronted, is serene and evasive. The emotional beat is betrayal's first sting: the man who taught Ulyana 'every grave deserves the truth' has been its most careful liar.

chapters.title: The Winter of '95
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Through Odile's reluctant, wine-loosened testimony, the truth of that winter emerges: Ada discovered the Trust's founding fortune was embezzled, and the five sealed her in the chapel crypt during a blizzard, telling themselves she'd be found. She wasn't. Ambrose certified her death as exposure, elsewhere. The beat is horrified pity — survival bought with a girl's life, then laundered into charity.

chapters.title: Anniversary Eve
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. The anonymous letters resume, each quoting the heirs' own alibi words back at them. Ulyana realizes the sender knows the phrasing because they wrote it: Ambrose coached the alibis and has spent thirty years curating his revenge. Ulyana tries to warn Sheriff Duane, who owes the Voss family too much to listen. The beat is isolation — the truth has no institution left to hold it.

chapters.title: A Glass Raised
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. At the anniversary dinner, Ulyana watches the heirs toast the Trust's legacy when the lights fail. In the dark, a gunshot; when power returns, Odile Voss is dead at the head of the table, an old chapel key in her hand. The beat is terror breaking into the open — the pattern is real, and Ulyana was meant to witness it.

chapters.title: The Pattern Completed
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Ulyana maps the deaths: Ambrose is working down the alibi list in the order the heirs spoke their lies that night, and Ivy Bellamy — who was a child in 1995, coerced into silence — is next. Racing the timeline, Ulyana finds Ambrose's confession letters, unsent, each one a eulogy for Ada. The beat is grim clarity: this was never chaos, only a coroner's final, meticulous autopsy of a town.

chapters.title: The Crypt Below the Chapel
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Climax. Ulyana reaches the crypt as Ambrose prepares to seal Ivy inside — recreating Ada's death so the town will finally have to look at it. He argues he is the only honest man left, that his certificate was the town's original sin. Ulyana talks him down with the one thing he can't refute: a proper inquest, his own doctrine. He surrenders Ada's remains to Ulyana's hands. The beat is devastating compassion.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Resolution. Ada Wrenlow is buried at last under her own name; the heirs face charges, the Trust dissolves, and Ulyana testifies against Ambrose, visiting him in custody with the old journals he'll now finish honestly. The final beat is the price of survival made plain: Ulyana keeps their post, knowing every grave by name, and adds one more — the town's innocence, buried beside the truth it killed to keep.
